Commentary.Commentary: So that is it from this series! Bangladesh creates history as they win their first bilateral series against Sri Lanka. The series though ended with a sour note for them as Sri Lanka ended the series with a comprehensive win and have lots of positives to take back home. We hope you enjoyed the coverage of the series. We look forward to seeing you for future games. Till then, goodbye and take care!

Kusal Perera, the Sri Lankan skipper, says that they needed a win and it is good to win here, and when he gets set while batting, then he looks to bat out there for a longer time. Feels that he took chances early on and when he got set, he tried to change his gears. Praises their bowling department and also opines that their fielding has been brilliant too and in the first two games, their batting let them down.

Mushfiqur Rahim, THE MAN OF THE SERIES, says that the boys worked really hard for this series and they came up with good plans and executed well. Feels that when you play 15+ years, you need to contribute more and more for your country and he looks to do that. Further praises Sri Lanka, as they always come hard. Adds that he enjoys the pressure while batting and he uses that to bat well.

Dushmantha Chameera, THE MAN OF THE MATCH, says that he is very happy with how he bowled, and coming back after losing the first two games was good. Tells that he was not under pressure coming into this series and he is relaxed. Adds that he is pleased with his role with Sri Lanka.

Tamim Iqbal, the Bangladesh skipper, says that they have won the series but feels that they did not play a complete game but opines that they need to work on a lot of areas. Says that Sri Lanka had an attacking mindset coming into the game and it worked out for them. Tells that the seniors are contributing big but he says that he believes in his youngsters and feels that if they start to perform well, then they will start playing better.

It was a complete performance from Sri Lanka. Earlier in the day, they won the toss and opted to bat. A decision that proved to be a good one. Skipper, Kusal Perera led from the front as the tourists managed to get to 286 on the back of a century from the skipper and a fifty from Dhananjaya de Silva. Taskin Ahmed was the pick of the bowler for Bangladesh as he managed to finish with a 4-fer but overall Bangladesh did not look good with the ball or in the field.

It was the Dushmantha Chameera show with the ball. As his pace and aggression proved to be too good for the Bangladeshi batsman. He derailed the Bangladesh chase even before it could get off the station. He finished with superb figures of 5/16 from his 9. The other bowlers followed suit. Wanindu Hasaranga and debutant Ramesh Mendis both got two wickets while Binura wrapped up his debut with a wicket as well.

Chasing 287, Bangladesh needed a solid start but that did not happen. They lost Naim, Shakib, and Tamim all in Powerplay 1 and with hardly any runs on the board. Mushfiqur and Mosaddek tried to steady the ship but the required run rate kept creeping up and that saw the pressure keep building. Mahmudullah and Mosaddek managed to get fifties but barring that, there was hardly anything to talk about.

A comprehensive win for Sri Lanka and they finish the series with a win and get their first win of World Cup Super League. Bangladesh will be disappointed with their performance with the bat as they never looked in the game with the bat.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Chameera strikes again and Sri Lanka snare another wicket. The Bangladeshi skipper, who has played well in this series, has been sent packing and Chameera is all over the batters here, as he gets his third wicket of the game. A slower and fuller ball outside off, Iqbal looks to push the ball to the off side, but only manages a thin outside edge, which is gobbled up nicely by Dickwella. An appeal and up goes the finger of the umpire. Iqbal does not hesitate in taking the review on this occasion. Ultra Edge rolls in and there is a thin spike as the ball goes past the bat and hence, the on-field decision stays on. The hosts in some trouble now. 259 needed from 243 balls.
Commentary.Howout: c Niroshan Dickwella b Dushmantha Chameera

Shortish and around off, slightly on the quicker side too, Shakib Al Hasan looks to pull but does not do so cleanly. Ramesh Mendis at square leg, backtracks slightly, and lunges to snare the ball out of thin air. A wonderful take and Chameera is on fire again. 278 needed in 282 balls.
Commentary.Howout: c Ramesh Mendis b Dushmantha Chameera

Commentary.Commentary: Around off, tapped to the off side.
Floated on the pads, tucked away to the square leg fielder.
Comes down the track and works this to mid on for a quick single.
On off, worked through mid-wicket for one.
WIDE. Slipped down the leg side. Wide signalled.
Loopy around off, milked to the long off fielder for one.
Loopy on the pads, nudged to the leg side for a single.
Flighted around off, Shakib eases this through mid off for a single.
Fuller and around off, this is pushed to mid off.
Shortish and outside off, Tamim Iqbal just leaves this one be.
Length and on off, Tamim keeps this one out.
Around off, this is tapped towards covers, for a quick single. Shakib Al Hasan is off the mark here!
Outside off, left alone.
Out comes Shakib Al Hasan at Number 3.

OUT! TAKEN! Chameera strikes on his first ball and the opening stand of Bangladesh has been torn apart very early on, in the run chase. Naim, who is playing in only his second ODI, makes no impact with the blade for the Tigers. A length ball, outside off, angling away from the left-hander here. Naim looks to go fishing and swings his blade, away from his body here, but only manages a thick outside edge this time. Kusal Mendis takes the catch at first slip.
Commentary.Howout: c Kusal Mendis b Dushmantha Chameera

Commentary.Commentary: Who will bowl now? Time for some pace now as Dushmantha Chameera will bowl now.
Shortish around off, tapped to the backward point fielder. 2 from the opening over!
Flighted on off, kept out.
Naim gets off the mark now. Loopy ball, outside off. Pushed down to long off for one.
Bangladesh and their skipper are underway! Fuller ball, on the pads. Tamim clips it towards deep square leg for one.
Flatter ball, on off. Tamim Iqbal looks to work it across the line but misses and gets hit on the pads.
Tossed up, in the line of the stumps. Tamim defends it out.
